claim: AI-assisted listings images emails and ads lower the cost of launching plausible event marketing
countervailingForce: Delivery quality and trusted brands remain scarce
leadingIndicator: New listing volume and registration-to-attendance by source
commercialImplication: Polished event content is no longer a meaningful moat
limitations: Eventbrite product claims do not prove operator profit

claim: AI can reduce bounded drafting scheduling and support work
countervailingForce: Competitors receive similar tools and errors require review
leadingIndicator: Minutes corrections and support outcomes per event
commercialImplication: Savings matter only when measured net of review and rework

claim: Conversational companions can substitute for some low-friction attention and social interaction
countervailingForce: Embodied reciprocal group participation offers a different outcome
leadingIndicator: Non-attender reasons chatbot use and paid-event substitution
commercialImplication: Do not assume either demand destruction or a loneliness tailwind
limitations: The study is US based lacks a no-chatbot control and is not an event-demand study

claim: Personal assistants can recommend and coordinate events without a marketplace browsing session
countervailingForce: Operators can distribute accurate inventory and earn direct return after attendance
leadingIndicator: Agent-referred bookings and direct sixty-day repeat
commercialImplication: Structured distribution helps but the agent may own discovery
limitations: Current UK booking adoption is unknown

claim: Agents may route bookings directly to venues or organisers and bypass discovery aggregators
countervailingForce: Owned programmes and direct attendee relationships remain valuable
leadingIndicator: Share of bookings transacted without marketplace visits
commercialImplication: Do not build a business whose sole asset is event aggregation
limitations: No retained source proves mature autonomous event purchasing

claim: Permissioned attendance repeat and format-outcome data can improve programming beyond public listings
countervailingForce: Data may remain sparse biased or too sensitive to use
leadingIndicator: Cohort depth correction rate and uplift from tested interventions
commercialImplication: Own consent-aware outcomes rather than generated compatibility prose
limitations: No first-party cohort has been collected

claim: Hosts venues travel and shared attendance remain physical constraints
countervailingForce: The same constraints create cost incidents and capacity risk
leadingIndicator: Show-up fill contribution and host or venue concentration
commercialImplication: Physical delivery resists replacement but must earn its burden
limitations: Durability does not prove attractive margin

claim: Synthetic promotional media and derivative speaker content increase provenance rights and misrepresentation risk
countervailingForce: Clear disclosure consent and retained provenance can preserve trust
leadingIndicator: Complaints rights incidents and synthetic-media disclosures
commercialImplication: Treat provenance and speaker permission as operating controls
limitations: The UK report is not event-specific legal advice

claim: Reliable hosts venues speakers and returning attendees remain relationship assets
countervailingForce: Incumbents may use scale to secure supply
leadingIndicator: Repeat venue terms host retention and direct attendee return
commercialImplication: Invest in the operating network rather than a model wrapper
limitations: No live fieldwork has verified retention

claim: Dependence on marketplaces social platforms or one recommendation agent leaves demand exposed
countervailingForce: Multi-channel distribution and direct return reduce concentration
leadingIndicator: Registration and repeat concentration by source
commercialImplication: Use marketplaces to start but build direct demand

claim: A locally dense repeatable programme can remain defensible when content tools commoditise
countervailingForce: Physical operations can destroy value if density and contribution fail
leadingIndicator: Sixty-day repeat contribution and concentration gates
commercialImplication: Proceed with a physical programme and reject AI-tool differentiation
limitations: The proposed moat has not been tested in a live cohort
